public_spec:
Title: Expiry handling with lead time

Behavior requirements:
- apply category lead time rules before deciding whether an item should be handled today
- if an item’s expiry date is today after lead time adjustment, return handle_today = true
- if an item’s expiry date is tomorrow or later after lead time adjustment, return handle_today = false by default
- invalid expiry dates must produce an error
- lead time adjustments should be derived from category_lead_time per policy_id inventory.expiry.lead_time

Edge cases:
- expiry date exactly today but negative or non-existent lead time should still be treated as today after rule application
- expiry date in the past with positive lead time should be considered invalid or produce error
- categories without explicit lead time rules default to no lead time (i.e., treat as today only if expiry is today)
- null or malformed date input should produce an error

Acceptance criteria:
- Expiring today returns handle_today = true after applying category lead time
- Expiring tomorrow returns handle_today = false after applying category lead time
- Invalid dates return an error

Non-goals:
- defining or altering lead time values themselves (policy dictates source of lead time)
- handling of items with expiry beyond a fixed horizon unless mandated by expiry date

Testable assertions:
- Given an item with expiry date = today and category with zero lead time, should_handle_today returns true
- Given an item with expiry date = today and category with positive lead time that shifts expiry to today after subtraction, should_handle_today returns true
- Given an item with expiry date = tomorrow after lead time adjustment, should_handle_today returns false
- Given an item with invalid expiry date, an error is returned
